raw_response:
Alright, let me think through the year as I always do.

---

*[Thinking as the farmer]*

At 65, with 40 years of cotton behind me, I don't experiment much anymore — what works, works. My 12 mu sits on the sandy loam that most of our village has, decent soil but not rich, and with just me and my wife at home the real constraint is labor, not land or money. The kids send us some cash but we want to keep pulling our own weight from this ground.

**Variety and planting.** I'll buy the same Bt hybrid I used last year from the agricultural supply shop in town, about 40 yuan per mu of seed. Not worth saving seed from a hybrid. Planting goes in the last week of April under plastic mulch — that's 35 yuan per mu for the film but it earns back the cost in faster emergence and fewer weeds. If a cold spell threatens I'll wait a few days; soil temperature matters more than the calendar.

**Fertilizer.** I target about 280 kg lint per mu — that's where my yield has sat pretty steady, and I see no reason to chase higher numbers at my age. Working from that target I put down roughly 15 kg N, 7 kg P₂O₅ and 9 kg K₂O per mu. In practice that's about 40 kg of compound fertilizer (45-15-15) broadcast before mulching, then a urea topdress of around 15 kg/mu at squaring in early July. If I see pale plants at flowering I'll do a foliar spray of KH₂PO₄ — cheap insurance against early senescence. I split N application because cotton takes it up over a long window, and one base shot alone gives you weak plants by August.

**Irrigation.** Two waterings for sure — once before planting to get uniform emergence, once at peak flowering in mid-July when bolls are setting. A third pass only if August stays dry. The tube well runs me about 40 yuan per mu per watering once you count electricity, and the meter doesn't care whether the sky delivers or not.

**Pest and weed control.** Acetochlor herbicide before laying mulch handles most weeds for the season. Even with Bt cotton, mirids and aphids will come — I budget 3 to 4 insecticide sprays over the season, mostly imidacloprid early and a pyrethroid mix later. No fungicide unless I see seedling disease after a cold wet spell.

**Tillage.** I hire the rotary tiller operator, about 60 yuan per mu including the mulch-laying pass. My back can't do that work anymore and it's not worth owning a machine for 12 mu.

**Labor — the hard one.** The two of us can do planting, spraying, weeding, and irrigating ourselves. Picking is impossible. I'll hire pickers for three rounds from late September through mid-October. Around here that runs about 1 yuan per jin of seed cotton, and at roughly 740 kg/mu seed cotton that's something like 300-400 yuan per mu just for picking. It's my single biggest cost.

**What could go wrong.** A bad mirid outbreak or a hailstorm in August are the usual worries. I keep some cash back — maybe 2,000 yuan — for an extra spray round or a rescue irrigation. I don't carry crop insurance; the local product doesn't cover much and the paperwork is more trouble than it's worth.
